title: Overseas Press Club concert album with Earl Hines
summary: A lunchtime concert at the Press Club with Earl Hines, whom she knew from Pittsburgh and saw with Louis Armstrong's group in 1952.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe

blocks.x: Okay. Shall we move on now to another of your fantastic successes. This is -- it's another live performance.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

It's the album you made at the Overseas Press Club in November 1970 with somebody from you home town. Yeah. With Earl Hines. Wilma Dobie, who is a very good friend of mine, she's been promoting these jazz sessions for a long time. She's a jazz fan from way back. And they decided to start a series of jazz performances called "Twilight Jazz," in 1970, I believe it was. And --
That's a good time of day to have a jazz concert, isn't it?
I wish they would do more.

It's a very good time of day. Well, in this particular case, people were getting off from work and they'd come right there. And they can get out early enough to go home, and still have their supper or whatever. And even if they wanted to go out later, they could do that.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

But anyway, Wilma is from Pittsburgh, too. So she knew Earl years ago and -- I think Wilma left Pittsburgh before I came to New York, and also before I went into the B.H.L. Club in Pittsburgh. But she didn't know too much about me until after I got to New York. But Earl Hines and I are honorary co-chairmen of the Overseas Press Club jazz club. And as her first twilight series, she had the both of us there. And I hadn't seen Earl for years.
In fact, as I recall, you say something -- you're quoted on the liner notes -- you say you had seen him in 1952, or something like that.

Yeah, when he was working with Louie Armstrong and his group. I was in Pittsburgh, I guess doing a nightclub performance in the early 50's. In Pittsburgh, there was a musicians club, and they usually invite -- they have celebrity night when
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
attractions are in town. And they had Louie there and I was a guest. And that's when I saw Earl for the first time since, oh boy, 1923.

Because Earl had naturally been all over the world by 1970. In fact, I had an uncle that appeared in a band that Earl Hines was in. The leader was Lois Deppe who was a singer. And the group was the Lois Deppe Serenaders.
They had made recordings as early as 1923. And I listened to them. My uncle, Harry Williams, was a drummer with the band.
And they made recordings on a label, Gennett Records. And we had those records.
